### [S049.U11] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
1. Weight batching shall be preferred at site but subject to the ER's approval it may be permit designed mixes to be converted to volumetric equivalents if requested in writing by the Contractor on specific grounds. The Contractor shall provide required boxes to measure the ingredients of concrete.
2. The Contractor shall provide concrete batch mixers, vibrators, weight batches conforming to relevant IS specification. The capacity and number of mixers and vibrators required at site from time to time shall be to the approval of the ER. No equipment from site shall be removed without the prior written approval of the ER. The Contractor shall also maintain a platform weighing scale of capacity 300 kg with fraction upto 100 gms at the site.

### [S049.U12] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
3. As directed by the ER, a weekly or periodic calibration of all machines shall be done and records of these calibrations shall be maintained in a register. Regular maintenance of machinery shall also be carried out on a weekly basis or as directed by the manufacturer of machines.
4. The mixer shall be run for a minimum period of 2 minutes after all materials are loaded in full quantity. The concrete produced shall be uniform in colour and consistency.

### [S049.U13] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
- a. Excessive mixing requiring the addition of water to preserve the required consistency shall not be permitted. Mix concrete to a consistency which can be readily placed without segregation.
- b. Equip mixers with a device for measuring and dispensing admixtures. When required, the slump of concrete may be increased prior to placement by the use of a high range water reducing admixture.

### [S049.U14] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
5. Hand-Mixed Concrete: When hand-mixed concrete is allowed and approved for certain parts of the Work, mix on watertight platforms. Proportion cement, sand and aggregate loose by volume, carefully measured. Thoroughly mix sand and cement together dry until the mixture is of uniform color. Add the aggregate and turn the

- mass over until the mixture is uniform and homogeneous. Add water by sprinkling and turn the mass over until it is uniformly mixed and of the required consistency.

### [S049.U15] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
6. Retempering: No water shall be added to the mix after the initial batching operation. Concrete which is placed after the unauthorized addition of water is subject to removal.
7. When required, the slump of concrete as delivered to the site may be increased prior to placement by the use of a high range water reducing admixture. Dosage of superplasticizer shall be within the guidelines established by the manufacturer and agreed to by the ER. Alternative Mix Design Reports with the recommended site dosage(s) of superplasticizer shall be submitted prior to use.

### [S049.U16] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > D. Mixing Of Concrete
8. The placing temperature of concrete shall not be more than 34 o C. If it is more, the ER may order addition of ice or chilled water to the concrete at no additional cost to the Employer. Also the Contractor shall take the following precautions:
- a. Mixers and weight batches shall be painted with white colour
- b. Aggregate storing bins shall not be exposed to the Sun.
- c. Water shall be sprinkled on aggregates well before concreting to keep the temperature low.

### [S051.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > F. Laying of Concrete > 1. Concreting shall commence only after formwork is approved, reinf...
3. Concrete shall be as gently deposited as is practically possible. In its final position to avoid re-handling and shall be so deposited that segregation of aggregates does not occur. In the case of deep trenches and footings, this may be done with the help of a chute.

Columns and walls shall be so adjusted in formwork so that maximum fall is 1.5

- meters unless consented to by the ER. Concrete from wheelbarrows shall not be dumped away from the face concrete already in place. It shall be dumped into the face of concrete already in place.

### [S051.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > F. Laying of Concrete > 1. Concreting shall commence only after formwork is approved, reinf...
4. Concrete placed onto a sloping surface shall be discharged by providing a chute with a baffle and a drop at its end so that the concrete remains on the slope.
5. Columns and walls shall be concreted in one operation to their full height to avoid any horizontal construction joints as far as possible.

### [S051.U4] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > F. Laying of Concrete > 1. Concreting shall commence only after formwork is approved, reinf...
6. All slabs, beams, wooden planks and cat-walks shall be provided clear of reinforcement. Concrete shall be placed in position within 30 minutes from the time it is produced. Concrete shall be laid during normal working hours. Concreting at night or on holidays shall be permitted only on the written approval of the ER.
7. Free Fall: Guide the flow of concrete in walls and columns for vertical drop between the reinforcing. Limit the free fall of concrete to maximum 2.5.m.

### [S052.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > G. Compaction of Concrete > 1. Concrete shall be thoroughly compacted, as depositing shall proc...
1. Concrete shall be thoroughly compacted, as depositing shall proceed by means of suitable vibrators. The vibrators shall maintain the entire concrete under treatment in an adequate state of agitation that shall continue during the whole period of placing of concrete. Care shall be taken not to over- vibrate the concrete. While withdrawing needles no holes shall be visible in concrete. Compacting shall be completed before the initial setting time. Concrete already set shall not be disturbed by successive vibrations.

### [S052.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > G. Compaction of Concrete > 1. Concrete shall be thoroughly compacted, as depositing shall proc...
2. Insert and withdraw vibrators vertically drawing out entrapped air and excess water. Do not use vibrators to transport concrete within forms. Do not insert vibrators into lower layers of concrete that have begun to set. At each insertion limit duration of vibration to time necessary to consolidate concrete and complete embedment of reinforcement and other embedded items without causing segregation of mix. Pay particular attention to providing adequate vibration in the vicinity of sleeves and embeds in heavily reinforced elements and other elements as required. Provide form vibrators to ensure maximum density of concrete.
3. It shall be ensured that the needle vibrators are not applied to reinforcement, which may destroy the bond between concrete and reinforcement. When electric vibrators are in use, a standby petrol vibrator shall always be available at the concreting point.

### [S053.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concreting continuously. Hence construction joints shall be provided. Location of construction joint shall be submitted by the Contractor for approval of the ER. Such joints shall be kept to a minimum. The joints shall be at places where shear forces are nil or minimum and these shall be straight and at right angles to the direction of the main reinforcement.

### [S053.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > H. Construction joints > 1. In large pours, it is practically not possible to carry on concr...
2. Form construction joints with a shear key. In walls, do not space construction joints more than 18m apart in horizontal direction, maximum 6m apart in vertical direction

- unless otherwise shown. In framed slabs and beams, and on metal deck slabs, do not space construction joints more than 27m apart. In slabs on grade, do not space construction joints more than maximum 18m in any direction. Place construction joints perpendicular to main reinforcement. Continue reinforcement across construction joints except as otherwise shown.

### [S054.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > L. Openings
- N. Curbs: Provide monolithic finish to interior curbs by stripping forms while concrete is still green and steel-troweling surfaces to a hard, dense finish with corners, intersections, and terminations slightly rounded.
- O. Equipment Bases and Foundations: Provide machine and equipment bases and foundations, as shown. Set anchor bolts for machines and equipment to template at correct elevations, complying with certified diagrams or templates of manufacturer furnishing machines and equipment.

### [S055.U1] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.6 CONCRETE > P. Curing
1. After concrete has begun to harden i.e. about 1 to 2 hours after placement, it shall be protected from quick drying with moist or damped Hessian cloth or any other material approved by the ER. Starting 24 hours after placement of the concrete, the surface shall be cured by flooding with water or covering with damp Hessian cloth for a period of 7 days to keep it moist.
2. For the next 7 days the surface shall be kept wet all the time by sprinkling water continuously.
3. For Mass Concrete: Curing period shall be 14 days.
4. For membrane curing, details as listed in 12.5 of SP 24 shall be followed.

### [S059.U5] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.9 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL > 7. Acceptance of Work
- A. Contractor's Quality Control Responsibilities: Contractor is solely responsible for quality control of the Work and shall develop and maintain a Quality Control Program for the Work.
- B. Certification: Certify, by written report submitted on a weekly basis, for each level, that the elevations, finish lines and building lines of the formwork systems are within specified tolerances, as substantiated by transit survey and that embedments and inserts have been installed within tolerance. Perform survey at locations indicated by the ER (minimum one per bay per floor) of formwork immediately before casting of concrete.

### [S060.U2] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- C. Monitoring of Concrete Placement: Continuously observe concrete placement operations on a full-time basis, record such observations on a daily basis, and submit reports of the results.
- D. Monitoring of Contractor's Testing: Monitor Contractor's non-destructive strength testing for form removal and termination of curing.

### [S060.U3] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING
- E. Compression Tests: Sample at point of deposit. Cure the cylinders in laboratory.
1. Additional Cylinders: Furnish a supply of 25 standard cylinder molds at the site at all times for making additional cylinders as may be directed by the ER.
2. Quantity of test cubes and testing
- a. The minimum frequency of cube casting for testing shall be as follows. Each sample shall consist of 6 cubes.

### [S060.U9] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- e. Compression Test Reports: Present at least the following data in tabular form and distribute immediately after recording the test results.
- 1) Identity of job, Contractor, supplier.
- 2) Identity of mix and required strength.
- 3) Pour location of sampled concrete.
- 4) Slump, water content, air content, truck number, time and date sampled, air temperature, concrete temperature, consistency.

### [S060.U10] PART 3 - EXECUTION > 3.10 INDEPENDENT TESTING > b. Three cubes shall be tested on the 7 th day and other three cube...
- 5) Curing history.
- 6) Date tested.
- 7) Compressive strength.
- 8) Type of fracture.
- 9) Compliance with specifications (yes or no)
- F. Slump Tests: First truck each day, each sample for cylinders, and as often as necessary thereafter. Provide a slump cone and rod available for use at all times. Verify water content in accordance with AASHTO T318, "Measurement of Water Content of Fresh Concrete Using the Microwave Oven" as required by the ER, but not less than one test per day.
